body:
Subject: Re: morning routine check-in

Jason -

Quick update since you asked last week: the 5:15 wake-up is sticking, mostly. Coffee, five minutes of quiet before Marcus is up, then I try to actually pray instead of just running my to-do list past God like He's my assistant principal. Some mornings win, some mornings Marcus is standing over me by 5:20 asking about dinosaurs.

The part that's actually helping is not touching my phone till after. Once email's open the calm is gone, obviously. Pastor Mitchell said something Sunday about margin before motion that I keep chewing on.

How's it going on your end - did the earlier wake-up survive contact with Karen's schedule, or did that fall apart by day three like mine usually does?

- Shanice

Subject: Re: morning routine check-in

Shanice -

Day three is generous, ours cratered by day two. Karen's still doing the early gym thing though, so I've got the house quiet for about twenty minutes most mornings and I'm trying to actually use it instead of scrolling.

Glad the no-phone rule is working for you - that tracks, you've always been better with a hard boundary than a soft goal. "Margin before motion" is a good line, stealing that.

Tell Marcus his dinosaur facts are always welcome interruptions. Talk soon.

- Jason

Subject: Re: Prayer and morning planning - follow-up

Jason,

Following up on what we talked about Sunday - I've moved my prayer time up to 5:15 so it's not getting swallowed by the Marcus-drop-off scramble. Two weeks in and it's actually sticking. Coffee first, then fifteen quiet minutes before the house wakes up, then the calendar sweep.

One thing I want your take on: should the morning planning block include Mom's Tuesday check-in calls, or does that muddy the "just me and God" part of it? You've got more practice compartmentalizing than I do.

Call me before you head to work if you get a sec.

- Shanice

Shanice,

Glad it's sticking - 5:15 is no joke though, don't burn yourself out being a morning miracle. My two cents: keep Mom's calls out of the prayer block. Let that stay just yours. Slot her into the planning half instead, right after, so it's still handled but doesn't compete for headspace.

I started doing something similar before work - nothing as structured as yours, but five minutes of quiet in the truck before I go in. Didn't expect it to help as much as it has.

Text me how the Tuesday split works once you try it. And eat something before you're out the door, I know how you get.

- Jason

Jason,

Tried the split this week - Mom's call slotted right after planning, and it worked better than I expected. Kept prayer time actually quiet for once. Pastor Mitchell would probably say I overcomplicated something that simple, but here we are.

Marcus is adjusting fine to the earlier wake-up too, mostly bribed by pancakes. Drop-off at Maple Hill's been smoother since I'm not rushing out the door mid-thought.

Thanks for talking it through with me - means more than you probably realize this week. Tell Karen I said hi.

- Shanice

Hey Jason,

Follow-up from this morning's sweep - can you double check the shared calendar? I've got two parent conferences and the Hartford Public Schools admin meeting all stacked at 3pm Thursday. Something's not syncing right on my end.

Also if you get a sec, mute the district-wide listserv threads from my inbox rules - they're burying the stuff I actually need to see before 7am. Marcus drop-off at Maple Hill is already eating my morning buffer, so I'd rather not be untangling email at the same time.

Thanks for jumping on this.

Shanice

Hey Shanice,

Looked at it - Thursday's a real conflict, not a display glitch. The admin meeting invite came in after your two conferences were already on there, so it just stacked instead of flagging. I moved the 3pm conference to 3:30 and left the other where it is. Let me know if that clashes with picking up Marcus.

Also set up the filter to route the listserv threads into a folder instead of the inbox - you'll still have them, just not first thing in the morning. Should make the sweep faster.

Hollering if anything else looks off.

Jason

Jason,

That works, 3:30 is fine - gives me a buffer before Maple Hill pickup. Thank you.

One more thing while you're in there: can you set a recurring block Mon-Fri, 6:45-7:15, labeled "do not book" for my morning sweep? People keep dropping meetings right into that window and I end up doing email triage during Marcus's drop-off instead of before it. Also loop in whoever handles the front office calendar so they stop scheduling over it.

Appreciate you handling this - feels good to walk into Bridgeport Avenue not already behind.

Shanice

Shanice,

Done - recurring block is on the shared calendar Mon-Fri 6:45-7:15, marked do-not-book, and I flagged it with the front office so it shows as unavailable on their end too. Also double-checked Thursday one more time, no other overlaps this week.

Listserv filter's live as of this morning, so tomorrow's sweep should already look cleaner. Ping me if the block gets ignored anyway - happens sometimes the first week.

Talk soon,
Jason

Jason,

Following up on the shelving in the book room - can you swing by Bridgeport Avenue Thursday after 3:30? I've got a staff meeting till then but the side door by the cafeteria will be propped. Just need the two units against the back wall, not the whole closet.

Also, if you're driving your truck, I could use help hauling the folding tables back to the gym - they've been sitting in the hallway since the PTO thing and the fire marshal will have opinions if they're still there at the walkthrough next week.

Let me know what time works. I'll be doing the Marcus pickup run around 4:45 so anything before that is easiest.

- Shanice

Shanice,

Thursday works, I'll head over around 3:45 with the truck. Should have the shelving done in under an hour, and I'll grab the tables while I'm there so you're not fighting the fire marshal over folding chairs.

Text me the side door code again if it's changed since last time - I forgot it walking up last month and had to loop around front like a visitor.

I'll be out before 4:45 so you're clear for Marcus. Talk Thursday.

- Jason

Subject: Re: Gmail API integration - still throwing errors

Jason,

Following up on the ticket from last week. The Gmail API sync we set up for the front office account (bavepta.frontoffice@) is still bouncing - every time it tries to pull new messages into the shared inbox it throws that invalid_grant error again. I'm doing my morning email sweep at 6:15 and it's just not populating.

Can you check if the refresh token expired again? This is the second time in a month and I've got staff meeting RSVPs and a field trip permission slip flood coming in that I actually need to see. If it's a scope issue, let's just fix it properly this time instead of a patch.

Let me know what you need from me - I can hop on a call after drop-off, around 8:15, once Marcus is settled at Maple Hill.

Thanks,
Shanice

Subject: Re: Gmail API integration - still throwing errors

Shanice,

Got it, pulled the logs. It is the refresh token - looks like the OAuth consent screen got bumped back to testing mode after the last update, which caps tokens at 7 days. That's why it keeps dying on you.

Two options: I publish the app properly for verification (takes a bit, Google review), or I add the front office account as a test user manually so tokens stop expiring in the meantime. I'd do the second now and start the verification process today so we're not back here in a month.

Can you confirm the exact email alias again - is it bavepta.frontoffice@hartfordschools.org or the .k12 domain? Want to make sure I don't set this up on the wrong tenant like last time.

Call works, I'll be free after 8. Talk then.

- Jason

Subject: Re: Gmail API integration - still throwing errors

Jason,

It's the .k12 domain - bavepta.frontoffice@hartfordschools.k12.ct.us. Same as always, just double check you're pulling from the district directory and not the old sandbox one.

Add it as a test user for now, that'll get us through the week. Go ahead and kick off verification too since apparently we're doing this every month. If Google needs a point of contact for the review, use my school email, not personal.

Appreciate you jumping on it fast - this is exactly why I call you first instead of opening a district IT ticket that sits for two weeks. I'll confirm on my end once messages start flowing again.

Talk soon,
Shanice

Hi Jason,

Following up on ticket #4471 - the Google Calendar API sync for Bridgeport Avenue's staff scheduling is still dropping events. Our front office feed connects fine, but recurring staff meetings pushed from our system aren't landing on the shared calendar. Third day in a row now and I've got a staff PD session Thursday that needs to show up correctly.

Can you check the sync logs on your end? I'm on-site most of the day but reachable by email between periods.

Thanks,
Shanice

Hi Shanice,

Thanks for the follow-up - I've got ticket #4471 pulled up. Before I dig into the sync logs, can you confirm a couple things: which calendar ID is the target (the shared staff calendar or your personal one), and roughly what time the Thursday PD session was created? Also, did you regenerate the OAuth token recently, or is this the same credential from setup?

That'll help me narrow down whether it's a scope issue, a token expiry, or something on the recurrence-rule side.

Best,
Jason

Jason,

Target is the shared staff calendar (bpe-staff@hartfordschools cal ID). Token hasn't been touched since setup back in the spring. The PD session was created yesterday around 7am when I did my morning email/calendar sweep - recurring weekly, Thursdays.

One more wrinkle: when I manually re-added it as a workaround, it duplicated instead of overwriting. Now I've got two entries every Thursday through the semester. Would rather not have my staff showing up confused about which one's real.

- Shanice

Hi Shanice,

Found it - the token was fine, but the recurrence rule was getting rejected silently because of a malformed RRULE from last spring's setup, which is why manual re-adds duplicated instead of updating. I've patched the rule handling and force-synced the calendar; the duplicates should be cleared out now on your end, with only the correct Thursday recurrence remaining.

Can you take a look when you get a chance and confirm the shared calendar looks right? If Thursday's PD session shows clean, I'll close out #4471.

Thanks for your patience on this one,
Jason

Hi Jason,

Following up on ticket #4471 - the Google Drive API integration for our shared staff folders is still throwing that 403 error when the sync tool tries to pull report card templates. Started Monday morning, still happening today.

I've got teachers who can't access shared lesson plan folders before first bell. Can you check if our API key or OAuth scope got reset on your end? Need this resolved before Friday's staff meeting if possible.

Thanks,
Shanice Giles
Principal, Bridgeport Avenue Elementary

Hi Shanice,

Thanks for the follow-up. Pulled the logs on ticket #4471 - the 403 was caused by a scope change on our end during a routine security update Monday night. Your API key's drive.readonly scope got dropped from the whitelist.

I've restored full drive.file and drive.readonly access and pushed the fix at 9:14 AM today. Can you have someone test the sync on one of the affected staff folders and confirm it's pulling through? Should be immediate, but sometimes cached tokens need a re-auth on the client side.

Apologies for the disruption before your staff meeting - flagging this as priority so it doesn't recur.

Best,
Jason Giles
Support

Hi Jason,

Following up on ticket #4471 - the WhatsApp API integration for parent notifications. Last I heard, the template approval was stuck with Meta and we were waiting on business verification to clear. Any movement?

I'd like to have this live before the first week of August. We're piloting it with two 3rd grade classrooms at Bridgeport Avenue before rolling out school-wide, and I don't want to be troubleshooting API errors during the first week of school on top of everything else.

Also - can you confirm the sandbox number is still active? I tested a broadcast message Friday morning before drop-off and it never went through.

Thanks,
Shanice

Hi Shanice,

Good timing - Meta cleared the business verification yesterday, so we're past that blocker. Two of your three message templates (attendance alert, general announcement) are approved. The third, "early dismissal notice," got flagged for review because of the wording around pickup instructions - Meta's bot reads it as a request for personal info. I'd recommend simplifying it and resubmitting; approval usually takes 24-48 hours after that.

On the sandbox number: that's likely why your Friday test failed. Sandbox tokens expire every 24 hours unless refreshed, and yours had lapsed. I've reissued a new one and sent it to this email separately - should be good for testing through the pilot.

Want me to hop on a quick call this week to walk through the webhook setup for delivery receipts? Might save you some back-and-forth.

Best,
Jason

Jason,

That works - resubmitted the dismissal template this morning with simpler language, we'll see. New sandbox token is in and the test broadcast went through clean this time, so we're good there.

No need for a call, I think I can handle the webhook config myself, but I'll flag you if I get stuck. If the third template clears by Friday we'll be fully set for the pilot launch.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on this - genuinely.

Shanice

Hey Jason,

Following up on what we talked about Sunday - I've actually stuck with the 5:15 wake-up for eight days straight now. Coffee, ten minutes of quiet, then I read whatever James sent from the men's/women's group study before Marcus is even up. It's the only part of my day nobody's knocking on my office door.

The piece I still haven't nailed is the prayer time bleeding into planning mode - I catch myself mentally drafting the staff memo instead of actually praying. Any tricks from your side, or is that just a me problem?

- Shanice

Hey Shanice,

Eight days is not nothing, don't undersell it. Karen and I do the same thing most mornings - she says the trick is writing the to-do list on an actual notepad BEFORE you sit down, so your brain isn't holding it hostage during the quiet part. Get it out of your head and onto paper first, then it can't sneak in.

Also - since Mom mentioned she's been up early too - maybe worth comparing notes with her. She's been doing the porch-and-coffee thing forever, might have something useful.

Proud of you for protecting that window, honestly. You run yourself ragged the rest of the day.

- Jason

That notepad trick actually worked this morning - wrote down "call the roofer about the gym" and two other things before I sat down, and for once my brain let it go. Ten full quiet minutes before Marcus was banging on the bathroom door asking for his shoes.

Gonna try the porch thing with Mom Saturday if the weather holds. Might be nice to not do this solo for once.

Thanks for actually giving me something usable instead of just "you got this."

- Shanice

Ha, I'll take that as high praise coming from you. Saturday porch sounds good - I'll tell Mom to put the good coffee out, not the decaf she tries to pass off on people.

Keep the streak going. And if the memo-brain creeps back in, just add it to the notepad and move on - it'll still be there when prayer time's over, deadlines aren't going anywhere.

Talk soon,
Jason

Subject: Re: Morning routine check-in

Hey Jason,

Quick follow-up on what we talked about Sunday - I moved prayer time back up to right after coffee instead of trying to squeeze it in after Marcus is out the door. Made a real difference this week. Three days out of five I actually got through my whole list before the 7:15 push to Maple Hill.

Still haven't nailed down a consistent spot for the planning piece though. Some days it's five minutes at the kitchen table, other days it's in the car line waiting to pull out. Curious what's working for you and Karen these days, if anything's changed since the boys started summer camp.

Talk soon,
Shanice

Subject: Re: Morning routine check-in

Hey Sis,

Glad the coffee-then-prayer swap is sticking - told you mornings go better when you're not rushing straight into the list. Karen and I ended up doing something similar, we just do it the night before now instead of morning. Ten minutes after the boys are down, we run through the next day together. Takes the pressure off the a.m. window entirely.

Might be worth trying that for the planning half at least, even if prayer stays a morning thing for you. Doesn't have to be the whole routine moved, just the parts that keep getting bumped by the car line.

Let me know how next week goes. And tell Marcus his uncle says hi.

Jason

Subject: Re: Calendar sweep - need you to grab something

Jason,

Quick one. During my morning sweep I saw the district pushed the PD half-day to next Friday but nobody updated the master calendar - parents are going to show up expecting dismissal at 12:30 like normal. Can you call the front office and have them fix it before end of day? I'm back-to-back with a parent conference and an IEP meeting till 3.

Also if you talk to Mom before I do, don't mention the half-day thing, she'll want to plan around it for Marcus and I haven't figured out coverage yet.

Thanks,
Shanice

Subject: Re: Calendar sweep - need you to grab something

Hey Shanice,

Done - called the office around 9:15, they're pushing the corrected calendar out in the afternoon blast. I also flagged it to Karen since she does pickup for her two on Fridays sometimes, figured better safe than sorry.

One thing on my end: did you see the email from the district about the budget line reallocation? It landed in your inbox this morning too, might be worth a look before your IEP meeting eats your whole afternoon.

How'd the parent conference go, by the way?

- Jason

Subject: Re: Calendar sweep - need you to grab something

Jason,

Conference went fine, mostly logistics. Saw the budget email, already forwarded it to my assistant principal to draft a response - I'll review before it goes out tomorrow morning during my email sweep.

Appreciate you looping in Karen, that's one less thing on my plate. I'll swing by Mom's after Marcus's drop-off at Maple Hill tomorrow so we can catch up properly.

Talk soon,
Shanice

Jason - quick follow-up from today's walkthrough at Bridgeport Ave. The facilities guy still hasn't fixed the leak by the gym, and I need someone to loop in maintenance before the assembly Thursday. Can you flag it with whoever handles building requests on your end?

Also, thank you for swinging by yesterday - the staff noticed, and so did I. Running on fumes and Dunkin' this week but we're upright.

- Shanice

Hey Shanice - on it. I'll call facilities first thing tomorrow and cc you so you're not chasing anyone. Gym leak before Thursday's assembly is doable if they move fast.

Glad the visit helped. You looked like you needed someone to just show up and not ask for anything, so that was the plan. How'd drop-off go this morning, everything smooth with Marcus?

Talk soon - Jason

Drop-off was fine, thanks for asking. Maple Hill had their usual chaos but nothing new.

Update on the leak: facilities came by, patched it temporary-style, says permanent fix needs a work order approved higher up. I'll push that through admin myself Monday. Assembly should be fine either way - just don't let anyone walk under that corner in dress shoes.

One more thing - can you check if the district portal is still flagging Bridgeport Ave for the fire drill paperwork? I submitted it twice.

- S

Checked the portal - it was a submission glitch on their end, not yours. I got it manually marked complete, so Bridgeport Ave should be clear now. Screenshot the confirmation just in case they "lose" it again.

Good to hear about Marcus. And noted on the dress shoes - I'll pass the warning along like it's classified intel.

Proud of how you're juggling all this, sis. Let me know if the work order stalls and I'll nudge again.

- Jason
